sources.title: Bunyoro
sources.note: Founded late 16th century by Rukidi-Mpuga; 80,000 km2 at its 17th-century peak; Kooki and Buddu lost to Buganda; Tooro separates in the 1830s; Rwangabi 1886; Kabalega captured and Bunyoro annexed 1899; 1964 referendum.

sources.title: Toro Kingdom
sources.note: Founded 1830 by Olimi I; absorbed into Bunyoro 1876; interregnum reverted to Bunyoro 1880-1891; independence reasserted 1891; reign list; abolished 1967, reinstated 1993.

notes:
New state (Cliopatria has no Bunyoro row). The Bunyoro page is the only source; the Uganda Protectorate page adds the 1894 protectorate and the 1907 revolt (cited in notes only).

Not on the page, so not recorded: Rukidi's date (the c. 1500 of other works), the Bachwezi and Kitara empire before him, Kabalega's reign dates (1870-1899) and the April 1899 capture date, the wars with Ankole and Rwanda, the capital moves (undated), the lost counties' transfer to Buganda (undated; Buyaga and Bugangaizi were returned by a 1964 referendum, and the page names no 1900 transfer), Buwekula and Bugerere. Placeholder years (1590, 1800, 1830) are confidence 1 and each is flagged in its note.

The 80,000 km2 peak is the page's figure; the shape drawn is the researcher's union of districts. The kingdom was forcefully disbanded in 1967 and restored in 1993 (outside the life span).
